title: Reverse Bits
prompt: Reverse the bits of a given 32-bit unsigned integer `n` and return the resulting unsigned integer.

examples.explanation: Reversing the 32 bits of the input gives binary 00111001011110000010100101000000, which is 964176192.
Reversing the 32 bits gives binary 10111111111111111111111111111111, which is 3221225471.

constraints: The input is a 32-bit unsigned integer represented as a Python int in [0, 2^32 - 1]
hints: Think of the input as a fixed-width, 32-character binary string — reversal just flips the order of those characters.
You can build the result bit by bit: examine the lowest bit of n, and place it at the highest available position of the result.
Loop 32 times: shift the result left by one, OR in the lowest bit of n, then shift n right by one to expose the next bit.

solution.approach: Process all 32 bits one at a time. On each of 32 iterations, shift the accumulated result left by one bit to make room, then OR in the current lowest bit of n (n & 1), and finally shift n right by one to expose the next bit for the following iteration. After 32 iterations, the result holds the bits of n in reversed order.
